notes: MCP TOOLS. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first: implement `Tool` for each tool (`def()` returns `ToolDef::new("<name>", "<description>", <schema>)` with the name as a string literal at that call, the description copied verbatim from the TypeScript because it is prompt text, and the schema being the zod schema converted to JSON Schema: same property names, types, enums, defaults, limits, descriptions and required list), and expose `pub fn register(registry: &mut ToolRegistry)` from lib.rs that registers every tool of this crate. Output text must equal the TypeScript's: same wording, same JSON shape and key order (JSON.stringify(x, null, 2) corresponds to serde_json::to_string_pretty; serde_json's preserve_order feature is enabled in this crate, keep it). State the TypeScript keeps in module variables goes in a struct fetched with `ctx.state::<T>()`. The traffic store is `ctx.traffic`; script search, bundler detection and the webcrack runner are already ported in rever-analysis (script_analysis, grep_worker), exec-trace and listeners formatting and the script registry in rever-formats: use them as path dependencies. tools/scripts.ts compiles an agent-supplied JavaScript regex (pattern plus flags) before searching: translate it to the Rust regex crate (flags i, m, s; reject with a clear error what cannot be expressed, such as lookaround and backreferences). wasm-analysis.ts uses the wabt npm package and spawns its binaries: use Rust crates instead (wasmparser and wasmprinter for WAT and sections; for the C-like decompile and wasm2c outputs, shell out to `wasm-decompile` / `wasm2c` if they are on PATH and otherwise return the same kind of clear install hint the TypeScript gives), keeping function names, limits and output formats. sourcemap.ts fetches source maps over HTTP: use reqwest with rustls-tls. Tools that read the page (exec_trace, listeners, crypto_trace) use `ctx.browser`: `evaluate`, `add_init_script`, `remove_init_script`; where the TypeScript needs a Chrome DevTools Protocol feature with no `Browser` method (Debugger, Profiler coverage, DOMDebugger), do NOT edit rever-tools-api: return `utils::err(tool::unsupported("<what>"))` from that path, keep validation and pure logic, and list it under behaviorDifferences. Async: `call` returns a boxed future run on a tokio runtime; tests use #[tokio::test] and a fake `Browser` written in the test module. A tool file gets the `Port of` marker when all of its tools are registered.
